entries.title: Tomato leaf spot management
entries.answer:
Early blight and septoria leaf spot cause dark spots on tomato leaves. Remove infected leaves, avoid overhead irrigation before rain, and use copper-based fungicide if disease pressure is high. Treatment cost is typically moderate; delay sprays if heavy rain is forecast within 24 hours.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Tomato fertilizer rules
entries.answer:
Tomato needs balanced NPK. Excess nitrogen increases foliage and disease risk. Prefer split fertilizer doses. With limited budget, prioritize potassium and calcium during fruiting over additional nitrogen.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Tomato selling and storage
entries.answer:
Tomato is perishable with short shelf life. If mandi prices are falling and storage or cold chain is unavailable, consider staged early harvest of ripe fruit rather than holding for a recovery that may not come.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Tomato harvest timing
entries.answer:
Harvest at breaker to pink stage for distant markets; fully ripe for local sale. Morning harvest reduces heat stress. Sort by grade before transport — damaged fruit lowers overall mandi realisation.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Potato late blight
entries.answer:
Late blight thrives in cool wet weather. Scout lower leaves, destroy infected haulms, and apply approved fungicide preventively when rain is expected. Do not spray immediately before heavy rainfall.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Potato soil and NPK
entries.answer:
Potato prefers well-drained loamy soil. Maintain adequate potassium for tuber quality. Avoid waterlogging which raises disease and reduces marketable yield.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Potato storage basics
entries.answer:
Cure tubers in shade for 7–10 days before storage. Store in ventilated structures at 2–4°C if cold storage is available. Sprouting and weight loss increase above 8°C. Check PMFBY coverage before storing large volumes.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Onion thrips and bulb quality
entries.answer:
Thrips cause silvery streaks on leaves and reduce bulb size. Scout weekly during dry spells. Staggered planting reduces peak pest pressure. Harvest when 50–75% tops fall naturally for best storage life.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Onion price volatility
entries.answer:
Onion prices swing sharply with arrival volumes. When prices spike, graded sorting and proper curing improve realisation. During glut, consider value addition (drying) or staggered release if storage is available.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Maize nutrient deficiency
entries.answer:
Yellowing of lower leaves often indicates nitrogen deficiency. Apply urea in splits. Confirm soil moisture before top dressing. Maize responds poorly to drought at tasseling.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Maize fall armyworm basics
entries.answer:
Scout whorls for larvae. Early detection allows mechanical control or targeted insecticide. Avoid blanket sprays when beneficial insects are active.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Wheat rust management
entries.answer:
Yellow and brown rust spread in cool humid conditions. Use resistant varieties where available. Apply fungicide at flag leaf stage if disease exceeds economic threshold. NFSM districts may offer subsidized inputs — check locally.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Wheat irrigation critical stages
entries.answer:
Crown root initiation, tillering, jointing, flowering, and grain filling are sensitive to water stress. One missed irrigation at flowering can cut yield 15–25%. Skip irrigation only when rain exceeds 15 mm.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Rice transplanting window
entries.answer:
Transplant 25–30 day old seedlings at 2–3 seedlings per hill. Maintain 2–5 cm standing water during tillering. Drain briefly before panicle initiation to strengthen roots.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Rice stem borer scouting
entries.answer:
Dead hearts in vegetative stage and white ears at heading indicate stem borer. Monitor weekly. Release Trichogramma egg parasitoids where available before resorting to chemical control.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Cotton aphid and whitefly
entries.answer:
Honeydew from aphids leads to sooty mould. Whitefly transmits leaf curl virus. Avoid repeated broad-spectrum sprays that kill natural enemies. Rotate insecticide modes of action.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Irrigation and rain timing
entries.answer:
Skip irrigation when significant rainfall is forecast. Standing water increases fungal disease risk for tomato and potato. Schedule sprays after rain when leaves dry.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Drip irrigation benefits
entries.answer:
Drip saves 30–50% water versus flood irrigation and reduces weed pressure. PMKSY offers 45–55% subsidy on micro-irrigation. Pair drip with fertigation for better nutrient use efficiency on horticulture crops.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Limited budget decision rule
entries.answer:
Under tight budget, compare treatment cost against expected salvageable yield and current mandi price. If expected post-treatment profit is negative and prices are falling, selling early or reducing input intensity may be safer than full treatment.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Soil Health Card usage
entries.answer:
Test soil every 2 years through the Soil Health Card scheme. Apply nutrients based on recommendations rather than habit. Over-application of nitrogen is a common profit leak on small farms.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Crop insurance before risky decisions
entries.answer:
Enroll in PMFBY before sowing notified crops. Insurance does not replace good agronomy but limits downside when weather or pest causes total loss. Premium is heavily subsidized for most food crops.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Sprayer equipment guidance
entries.answer:
For small farms under 3 acres, knapsack or rental battery sprayers are usually more cost-effective than owning tractor-mounted sprayers. Factor rental into treatment cost.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Greenhouse and polyhouse government subsidy (India)
entries.answer:
Under MIDH/NHM, farmers can get credit-linked back-ended subsidy for polyhouses, greenhouses, and shade-net houses. Baseline central support is often about 50% of admissible project cost for private farmers; many states add top-ups so effective support can be higher for SC/ST, small/marginal, or hilly-area farmers. Application is through the District Horticulture Officer or state horticulture portal. A bank loan is usually required. Subsidy is typically released after construction and inspection, not upfront. Area limits and exact percentages vary by state — confirm on your state horticulture website before applying.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: Reducing post-harvest losses
entries.answer:
Sort and grade at harvest. Use clean crates, avoid stacking beyond 4 layers for tomatoes. Cold storage or AIF-backed warehouse loans can improve holding capacity when prices are depressed at peak arrival.

(Offline tip from Krishi AI crop knowledge. Confirm spray/dose with your local KVK when online.)

entries.title: PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi
entries.answer:
₹6000/year in 3 installments of ₹2000 Eligibility: All land-holding farmer families Apply: Register at pmkisan.gov.in or through CSC/local agriculture office More: https://pmkisan.gov.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
entries.answer:
Crop insurance at 2% premium (kharif), 1.5% (rabi), 5% (horticulture). Govt pays remaining premium. Eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas Apply: Through bank (loan farmers auto-enrolled) or CSC portal More: https://pmfby.gov.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) - Per Drop More Crop
entries.answer:
55% subsidy for small/marginal farmers, 45% for others on micro-irrigation (drip/sprinkler) Eligibility: All farmers; higher subsidy for SC/ST/small/marginal Apply: Apply through state agriculture/horticulture department More: https://pmksy.gov.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: PM-KUSUM (Solar Pump Scheme)
entries.answer:
60% subsidy (30% central + 30% state) on solar pumps up to 7.5 HP Eligibility: All farmers with grid-connected or off-grid pump needs Apply: Apply through state DISCOM or agriculture department portal More: https://mnre.gov.in/solar/schemes

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM)
entries.answer:
40-50% subsidy on farm machinery (tractors excluded); Custom Hiring Centres promoted Eligibility: Individual farmers, FPOs, cooperatives, panchayats Apply: Apply at agrimachinery.nic.in More: https://agrimachinery.nic.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: Soil Health Card Scheme
entries.answer:
Free soil testing and nutrient recommendations every 2 years Eligibility: All farmers Apply: Visit nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra or agriculture office More: https://soilhealth.dac.gov.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: National Food Security Mission (NFSM)
entries.answer:
Subsidized seeds, micronutrients, demonstrations, and equipment for rice/wheat/pulses/coarse cereals Eligibility: Farmers in identified districts growing target crops Apply: Through district agriculture officer More: https://nfsm.gov.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)
entries.answer:
Subsidy on planting material, drip, shade nets, polyhouse/greenhouse, cold storage, pack houses for horticulture crops Eligibility: Farmers growing fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, plantation crops Apply: Through state horticulture department More: https://midh.gov.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: MIDH — Polyhouse / Greenhouse / Protected Cultivation Subsidy
entries.answer:
Typically 50% credit-linked back-ended subsidy on admissible project cost for private farmers (baseline under MIDH/NHM). States may add top-ups (often 65–95% total for SC/ST, small/marginal, or hilly areas). Covers naturally ventilated polyhouses, fan-and-pad greenhouses, and shade-net houses. Eligibility: Farmers, FPOs, cooperatives setting up protected cultivation for horticulture crops. Area norms commonly 500–4,000 sqm per beneficiary under NHM (verify with state). Bank loan usually required (credit-linked). Apply: Apply through District Horticulture Officer (DHO) or state horticulture portal (e.g. MahaDBT in Maharashtra, HORTNET in Haryana). Submit land records, bank loan sanction if required, and project estimate. Subsidy is usually released after construction and joint inspection. More: https://midh.gov.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: National Horticulture Board (NHB) — Protected Cultivation
entries.answer:
Credit-linked back-ended subsidy (commonly 50% of project cost) for commercial polyhouse/greenhouse projects. Higher support possible in NE/Himalayan/hilly areas per NHB norms. Eligibility: Farmers and horticulture entrepreneurs; larger commercial units (often 2,500+ sqm depending on component). Credit linkage typically required. Apply: Apply via NHB/MIDH channels through approved bank loan and DHO/NHB procedure More: https://nhb.gov.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: MGNREGA - Farm-related Works
entries.answer:
100 days guaranteed wage employment; farm ponds, land leveling, plantation work covered Eligibility: Rural households with job card Apply: Apply to Gram Panchayat with job card More: https://nrega.nic.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
entries.answer:
3% interest subvention on loans up to ₹2 crore for post-harvest infrastructure (cold storage, warehouses, sorting) Eligibility: Farmers, FPOs, APMC, startups, cooperatives Apply: Apply through banks on agriinfra.dac.gov.in More: https://agriinfra.dac.gov.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP)
entries.answer:
Training, resources, and support for women in agriculture; organic farming promotion Eligibility: Women farmers / SHGs Apply: Through state rural livelihood missions / NRLM More: https://nrlm.gov.in

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: Interest Subvention on KCC Crop Loans
entries.answer:
2% interest subvention + 3% prompt repayment incentive → effective 4% on crop loans up to ₹3 lakh Eligibility: All farmers with KCC Apply: Automatically applied to eligible KCC accounts More: https://www.nabard.org

(Offline scheme summary. Verify current rates on the official portal when online.)

entries.title: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) — Crop Loan
entries.answer:
Effective ~4% with subvention (listed 7%). Up to ₹3,00,000. Eligibility: All farmers (owner cultivators, tenant farmers, sharecroppers, SHGs). Apply: Any scheduled commercial bank, cooperative bank, or regional rural bank. Documents: Land records / tenancy proof, ID proof (Aadhaar), Passport photo, Crop plan. Repayment: Up to 12 months (crop season).

(Offline loan orientation. Bank terms may vary — confirm when online.)

entries.title: KCC — Term Loan (Allied Activities)
entries.answer:
Interest ~9%. Up to ₹2,00,000. Eligibility: Farmers with dairy, poultry, fishery, sericulture activities. Apply: Banks issuing KCC. Documents: KCC account, Project report for allied activity, Land/asset proof. Repayment: 3-5 years.

(Offline loan orientation. Bank terms may vary — confirm when online.)

entries.title: Agricultural Gold Loan
entries.answer:
Interest ~7.5%. Up to ₹25,00,000. Eligibility: Any farmer needing quick crop finance. Apply: SBI, cooperative banks, NBFC (Manappuram, Muthoot). Documents: Gold for pledge, ID proof, Land record (optional). Repayment: 6-12 months.

(Offline loan orientation. Bank terms may vary — confirm when online.)

entries.title: Farm Mechanization Loan (Tractor / Equipment)
entries.answer:
Interest ~9.5%. Up to ₹15,00,000. Eligibility: Farmers with minimum 2 acres or custom hiring centres. Apply: SBI, HDFC, ICICI, cooperative banks, NABARD-refinanced RRBs. Documents: Quotation from dealer, Land records, ID + address proof, Photos. Repayment: 5-7 years (EMI).

(Offline loan orientation. Bank terms may vary — confirm when online.)

entries.title: NABARD Dairy Entrepreneurship Loan
entries.answer:
Interest ~10%. Up to ₹7,00,000. Eligibility: Farmers, SHGs, entrepreneurs for dairy units (up to 10 animals). Apply: Banks refinanced by NABARD. Documents: Project report, Land / shed proof, Veterinary certificate. Repayment: 5-7 years.

(Offline loan orientation. Bank terms may vary — confirm when online.)

entries.title: MUDRA Loan — Shishu/Kishore (Agri-allied)
entries.answer:
Interest ~10%. Up to ₹5,00,000. Eligibility: Small/marginal farmers for agri-processing, trading, services. Apply: Any bank, NBFC, MFI under PMMY. Documents: Business plan, ID proof, Address proof. Repayment: 3-5 years.

(Offline loan orientation. Bank terms may vary — confirm when online.)

entries.title: Solar Pump Finance (PM-KUSUM linked)
entries.answer:
Interest ~8%. Up to ₹3,00,000. Eligibility: Farmers applying under PM-KUSUM Component B/C. Apply: NABARD-linked banks, state DISCOM facilitated. Documents: PM-KUSUM sanction letter, Land proof, ID proof. Repayment: 5-7 years.

(Offline loan orientation. Bank terms may vary — confirm when online.)

entries.title: Warehouse Receipt Loan (Pledge Finance)
entries.answer:
Interest ~7%.  Eligibility: Farmers storing produce in WDRA-registered warehouses. Apply: Banks with warehouse finance scheme. Documents: Warehouse receipt (negotiable), ID proof, Quality certificate. Repayment: Up to 6 months.

(Offline loan orientation. Bank terms may vary — confirm when online.)
